newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on $6 bln prepayment news.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on $6 bln prepayment news.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firm for the seventh session in a row on Tuesday due to an inflow of dollars to the market which followed an announcement Mexico will prepay $6 billion in debt, dealers said.
"The prepayment news, U.S. consumer price data, domestic industrial output, it was all very positive," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 2.0 and 1.9 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.9270/7.9300 and 7.9240/7.9270 per dollar.
"Foreign traders executed stop losses when the peso went below 7.94 per dollar, which is why it suddenly firmed to 7.93," the trader added.
Same-day peso contracts closed mid-morning 1.2 centavos firmer at 7.9360/7.9390 per dollar.
The Finance Ministry (Hacienda) announced Tuesday morning that Mexico will exercise an option to prepay an entire issue of $6 billion in floating rate bank notes placed Aug. 5, 1996.
Hacienda also announced industrial output in April had increased by 15 percent compared to the same month in 1996.
Dealers said the peso could cede some of its recent gains from the dollar on Wednesday if primary Cetes rates fell across the board at the central bank's primary auction to be held later in the day.
